_comment: One open Payment Mandate over the built scenario's four constraints, pinned
twice: as the user signed it, and as a Shopping Agent presents it to a
Credential Provider. The pair is the vector — either string alone says
nothing about minimisation, and the difference between them is the whole of
what issue #14 adds.
The two share an issuer-signed JWT character for character. Narrowing
removes disclosures and never re-signs, so a Credential Provider verifies
the same signature over the same digests; the two withheld constraints stay
in the payload as digests matching nothing, which RFC 9901 s7.1 step 3.d
removes from the array rather than leaving a hole.
withheld_for_the_credential_provider names what goes and why. AP2 sends that
role the Payment Mandate and nothing else, so it holds an amount, a payee
and its own clock and can state no fact about an item. The route is enforced
by the Merchant, out of the open Checkout Mandate, and the Credential
Provider never learns where the user is flying.
What this vector does NOT hide, and the implementation depends on it not
hiding: the number of constraints. Split either string on '~' and the
disclosures are countable; decode the issuer JWT and the constraints array
holds four digests in both. A Credential Provider therefore knows two were
withheld from it and which positions they held. It cannot learn what they
said. It cannot tell a withheld constraint from a decoy in general either —
but that defence does not apply to this array, because pkg/sdjwt puts decoys
in _sd arrays only and never in arrays of values, so for a mandate minted
here the count is exact. ap2's requireSomeConstraintDisclosed is what uses
it: a presentation that disclosed none of four is refused outright.
constraints. Split either string on '~' and the disclosures are countable;
Reproducing it needs the salts (newSalts) and the signer (hmacAuthzKey)
pinned together, for the reason testdata/open_checkout_mandate.json gives at
length: ECDSA draws a fresh nonce per signature, so a signed vector under
the key issuance actually uses could never hold.
Pinned by running TestGoldenMinimisedOpenPaymentMandate, reading the values
it produced, and confirming both in a second, separate `go test` process
before this file was committed.
